policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'Who soweth discord' with no wording that separates the qere plene מִדְיָנִים from the ketiv מדנים; both are the same word for strife/discord and yield identical English, and the single mapped note (hebrew_gloss, 'Hebrew letteth loose') glosses the verb of the preceding clause, not this lemma. Nothing in the verse distinguishes a reading, so both remain compatible and the qere base fallback carries the projection.

The candidates differ only in number, singular construct תּוֹעֲבַת against plural תועבות. ASV's 'Yea, seven which are an abomination unto him' does not settle this: with a numeral subject English idiomatically takes a singular predicate noun, so 'an abomination' is the natural rendering of either Hebrew, and the ASV does not gloss or note the number. The one mapped note (hebrew_gloss, 'Hebrew of his soul') explains the suffix rendered 'unto him' and is not classed textual_variant, so it cannot decide a reading. Both readings stand and the qere base fallback is retained.
